A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PhotoFramer. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite repagination and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original assessment-model experiments, GPT-5 and human evaluations of generated images, text-image consistency results, and qualitative ablations in Tables 2–4 and the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds assessment-baseline scores in Table 2 and iterative-refinement examples in Appendix Figure A1.

M1.justification: The Bagel-based architecture, losses, data-construction pipeline, task prompts, and two-stage inference remain unchanged. The new iterative examples test repeated application of the existing model without introducing a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: The same composition tasks, source datasets, and assessment benchmarks are retained. The iterative examples exercise existing composition-refinement tasks; they do not establish a new domain, dataset, or task requirement.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds VFN, VEN, and AutoPhoto to the assessment-model comparison. The main PhotoFramer comparator set remains unchanged. Renaming GPT-4o to gpt-image-1 does not introduce a comparator: v1 already identified that API in its footnote.

E3.justification: Appendix Figure A1 adds a qualitative testing procedure showing an original image followed by first and second edits for two examples. Existing splits, evaluation metrics, GPT-5/human judging, training budgets, and the 30-step generation setting remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds a qualitative investigation of whether one refinement round suffices and how successive rounds behave. Existing text-guidance and task-prompt ablations are retained. The painting failure case moves from Figure 13 to Figure A8.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate reporting without evaluation-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added comparisons and iterative examples introduce no uncertainty analysis.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds numerical results for VFN, VEN, and AutoPhoto; for example, AutoPhoto has AVA SRCC/PLCC of 0.604/0.613. Previously reported numerical results in Tables 2–4 remain unchanged. Figure A1 adds two qualitative iterative-refinement sequences.

T1.justification: The CPC score-model assumptions and derivations in Appendix B.1, Equations A1–A5, and the GRPO objective and rewards in Appendix B.2, Equations A6–A9, are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: hierarchical composition tasks, a curated multimodal dataset, and joint textual guidance and example-image generation. The added evidence does not redefine these core scientific claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly discusses compute and latency constraints on deploying the 14B model and defers robot validation. The retained painting failure is attributed broadly to limited datasets instead of specifically to excluding paintings. Appendix A adds discussion of single-round sufficiency and iterative reuse.

D1.justification: v2 newly states the 14B model size in Appendix C; existing implementation settings remain unchanged. The project URL is retained, but v1's explicit declaration that code, weights, and datasets are released is replaced by a generic project-page label. Actual resource availability is not established to have changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds AutoPhoto and Parametric Shadow Control for Portrait Generation as distinct cited works. AutoPhoto supports the assessment comparison and deployment discussion. Task decomposition is explicitly attributed to the already cited Freeman book; the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Localized edits standardize the gpt-image-1 name, add corresponding-author and acknowledgment information, and relocate the failure discussion to Appendix C. Several passages are refined, while the overall narrative and section organization are preserved.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains three baseline rows, Appendix Figure A1 adds iterative examples, and the painting failure figure moves into the appendix. Figures and text are resized or reflowed, with subsequent appendix figures renumbered; most visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: The additional assessment baselines in Table 2 modestly strengthen empirical validation, while the iterative examples and explicit deployment constraints clarify applicability. The gains remain limited because the iterative evidence is qualitative and the main results are unchanged. The less specific painting-failure explanation is a small countervailing loss.
